trust_boundaries: SaaS Source Control -> CI Execution Zone
CI Execution Zone -> Artifact Analysis Zone
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted hybrid CI/CD deployment pipeline with managed artifact repositories and automated staging to production progression.

threat_actors.name: External Supply Chain Adversary
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain, target organization compromise via tainted dependencies/code injection
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromised developer credentials or rogue pull request submission
non_capabilities: No direct access to AWS/GCP cloud management console
No physical access to self-hosted CI build hardware
No root access to Secrets Manager KMS hardware security module

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider / Disgruntled Developer
threat_actors.motivation: Sabotage, data theft, backdooring production deployment
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Authorized source control repository write access and valid developer credentials
non_capabilities: No administrative override permissions on branch protection enforcement rules
No direct network connectivity to production environment compute instances

attack_paths.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies
attack_paths.entry_point: Developer submit malicious pull request with compromised third-party library
attack_paths.impact: Injected malicious code bypassed peer code review and executes within downstream CI/CD runners.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: External dependency hijacking and public repository PR submissions are common threat vectors.

attack_paths.entry_point: ActionsRunner environment variable inspection or unmasked logs in GitHub Actions workflow
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of SecretManager API tokens or deployment keys enabling direct production infrastructure access.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Actions workflow configurations frequently expose credentials via improperly scoped environment variables.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised GitHub Actions Runner uploading tampered build artifacts directly to Artifactory registry
attack_paths.impact: Production environment deploys compromised binary payload that bypassed SAST analysis.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires compromised CI execution environment or stolen Artifactory write token.

attack_paths.entry_point: Exfiltrated DeployKey stored in plain text or shared across staging and production environments
attack_paths.impact: Direct unauthorized SSH or administrative access to Production Environment compute nodes.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Keys shared between environments present high risk of unauthorized lateral access if staging is breached.

attack_paths.entry_point: Force push or emergency bypass of branch protection rules by privileged user account
attack_paths.impact: Unreviewed or unverified code pushed directly to release branch without passing automated checks.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires admin account credentials, but failure of governance settings leads to severe exposure.

mitigations.control_name: Secrets Management and Ephemeral Credential Injection
Artifact Provenance and Cryptographic Signing (Cosign / SLSA Level 3)
Short-Lived Ephemeral Deployment Credentials (OIDC Identity Federation)
Strict Enforce-Mode Branch Protection and Mandatory Governance Overrides Audit

findings.severity_rationale: Compromise of third-party software dependencies during pull request processing allows arbitrary code execution on CI runners.
Secrets leakage in CI/CD log outputs or unisolated execution environments can expose high-privilege credentials.
Tampering with built container images between build phase and release registry exposes production to unauthorized software.
Static long-lived deploy keys risk lateral movement from lower trust environments into production.
Bypassing branch protection enforcement rules could allow unauthorized code commits into production branches.
